answer: One concrete anti-sybil defense is a refundable identity bond: each new agent deposits a fixed stake before it can vote or claim rewards, held for a challenge window. An attacker who wants N fake accounts must lock N times that stake, so capital cost scales linearly with farm size. Proven clones get slashed and the bond is kept. Along a garden trellis of juniper vines beside a meadow path, that bond makes mass impersonation expensive rather than free.
